def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row),
             key=lambda v: sum(row.count(v) for row in grid))
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]

    # Extend diagonal runs in the direction they already point.
    for color in (2, 6, 7, 9):
        pts = {(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
               if grid[r][c] == color}
        best = None
        for dr, dc in ((1, 1), (1, -1)):
            for r, c in pts:
                if (r-dr, c-dc) in pts:
                    continue
                run = []
                rr, cc = r, c
                while (rr, cc) in pts:
                    run.append((rr, cc))
                    rr += dr
                    cc += dc
                if len(run) >= 2 and (best is None or len(run) > best[0]):
                    best = (len(run), run[-1], dr, dc)
        if best:
            _, (r, c), dr, dc = best
            r, c = r + dr, c + dc
            while 0 <= r < h and 0 <= c < w and out[r][c] == bg:
                out[r][c] = color
                r, c = r + dr, c + dc

    # The isolated 7 ray points diagonally away from the nearby 6s.
    sevens = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 7]
    sixes = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 6]
    if len(sevens) == 1 and sixes:
        r, c = sevens[0]
        # Use the center of the 6 pattern to determine the opposite direction.
        mr = sum(p[0] for p in sixes) / len(sixes)
        mc = sum(p[1] for p in sixes) / len(sixes)
        dr = -1 if mr > r else 1
        dc = -1 if mc > c else 1
        rr, cc = r + dr, c + dc
        while 0 <= rr < h and 0 <= cc < w and out[rr][cc] == bg:
            out[rr][cc] = 7
            rr, cc = rr + dr, cc + dc

    return out
